```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(fpp2)
library(forecast)

candy <- read.csv("candy.csv")
candy_ts <- ts(candy$IPG3113N, start = c(1972, 1), frequency = 12)
```

## 1. Exploration

```{r}
summary(candy_ts)
plot(candy_ts, main = "US Candy Production Index (IPG3113N)", ylab = "Index")
lines(ma(candy_ts, order = 12), col = "red", lwd = 2)

Acf(candy_ts, lag.max = 48)
monthplot(candy_ts, ylab = "Index")
round(tapply(candy_ts, cycle(candy_ts), mean), 1)

ndiffs(candy_ts)
nsdiffs(candy_ts)
ndiffs(diff(candy_ts, 12))
tsdisplay(diff(candy_ts, 12))

stl_decomp <- stl(candy_ts, s.window = "periodic")
plot(stl_decomp)
round(window(stl_decomp$time.series[, "trend"], start = c(2024, 1)), 1)
```

**Insights:** the series has a strong yearly cycle (ACF of 0.89 at lag 12 and 0.83 at lag 24; production is about 26 index points higher in Oct–Dec than in Apr–Jul) and a long-run trend that rose until 2000, fell in 2008–09 and recovered. One seasonal difference makes it stationary (`nsdiffs` = 1, then `ndiffs` = 0). The STL trend peaked at about 100.5 in early 2025 and has fallen every month since, to 85.2 in August 2026. Jan–Aug 2026 output was 14% below Jan–Aug 2025.

## 2. Train / test split

```{r}
train <- window(candy_ts, end = c(2024, 8))
test  <- window(candy_ts, start = c(2024, 9))
h <- length(test)
```

The models are fit on Jan 1972 – Aug 2024 (632 months) and tested on Sep 2024 – Aug 2026 (24 months, two full seasonal cycles).

## 3. Models

```{r}
snaive_forecast <- snaive(train, h = h)

HW_model    <- HoltWinters(train)
c(HW_model$alpha, HW_model$beta, HW_model$gamma)
HW_forecast <- forecast(HW_model, h = h)

ets_model    <- ets(train)
ets_model
ets_forecast <- forecast(ets_model, h = h)

stl_forecast <- stlf(train, h = h)
stl_forecast$model$method

arima_model    <- auto.arima(train, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
arima_model
arima_forecast <- forecast(arima_model, h = h)

reg_model    <- tslm(train ~ trend + season)
summary(reg_model)$r.squared
reg_forecast <- forecast(reg_model, h = h)
```

## 4. Forecasts vs actual on the test set

```{r}
plot(test, ylim = c(70, 125), lwd = 3, main = "24-month forecasts vs actual", ylab = "Index")
lines(snaive_forecast$mean, col = "blue")
lines(HW_forecast$mean, col = "red")
lines(ets_forecast$mean, col = "green")
lines(stl_forecast$mean, col = "purple")
lines(arima_forecast$mean, col = "orange", lwd = 2)
lines(reg_forecast$mean, col = "cyan")
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Actual", "Seasonal naive", "Holt-Winters", "ETS",
                                "STL + ETS", "ARIMA", "Regression"),
       col = c("black", "blue", "red", "green", "purple", "orange", "cyan"),
       lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

## 5. Accuracy

RMSE is the selection measure: it is in index points, like the data, and it penalizes large misses, which are the costly ones for production planning. MAPE is shown as a percentage for management.

```{r}
acc_table <- rbind(
  "Seasonal naive" = accuracy(snaive_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")],
  "Holt-Winters"   = accuracy(HW_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")],
  "ETS"            = accuracy(ets_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")],
  "STL + ETS"      = accuracy(stl_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")],
  "ARIMA"          = accuracy(arima_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")],
  "Regression"     = accuracy(reg_forecast, test)["Test set", c("RMSE", "MAE", "MAPE", "MASE")]
)
round(acc_table, 2)
```

One 24-month test is dominated by the 2026 drop, so each model is also tested on ten separate years: train through August of year *k*, forecast the next 12 months, for *k* = 2016 to 2025.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
rolling <- NULL
for (k in 2016:2025) {
  tr <- window(candy_ts, end = c(k, 8))
  te <- window(candy_ts, start = c(k, 9), end = c(k + 1, 8))
  f <- list(
    "Seasonal naive" = snaive(tr, h = 12)$mean,
    "Holt-Winters"   = forecast(HoltWinters(tr), h = 12)$mean,
    "ETS"            = forecast(ets(tr), h = 12)$mean,
    "STL + ETS"      = stlf(tr, h = 12)$mean,
    "ARIMA"          = forecast(auto.arima(tr), h = 12)$mean,
    "Regression"     = forecast(tslm(tr ~ trend + season), h = 12)$mean
  )
  rolling <- rbind(rolling, sapply(f, function(p) sqrt(mean((as.numeric(te) - as.numeric(p))^2))))
}
rownames(rolling) <- paste0(2016:2025, "-", 2017:2026)
round(rolling, 2)
round(colMeans(rolling), 2)
```

## 6. Residual analysis

```{r, fig.height=8}
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
Acf(residuals(snaive_forecast), main = "Seasonal naive")
Acf(residuals(HW_forecast), main = "Holt-Winters")
Acf(residuals(ets_forecast), main = "ETS")
Acf(residuals(stl_forecast), main = "STL + ETS")
Acf(residuals(arima_forecast), main = "ARIMA")
Acf(residuals(reg_forecast), main = "Regression")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

Box.test(residuals(snaive_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung")
Box.test(residuals(HW_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung", fitdf = 3)
Box.test(residuals(ets_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung", fitdf = 2)
Box.test(residuals(stl_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung", fitdf = 1)
Box.test(residuals(arima_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung", fitdf = 5)
Box.test(residuals(reg_forecast), lag = 24, type = "Ljung")
```

## 7. Final model and forecast

```{r}
final_fit <- auto.arima(candy_ts, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
final_fit
checkresiduals(final_fit)

final_forecast <- forecast(final_fit, h = 12)
final_forecast
plot(final_forecast, include = 48, main = "ARIMA forecast, Sep 2026 - Aug 2027", ylab = "Index")

mean(final_forecast$mean)
mean(window(candy_ts, start = c(2025, 9)))
mean(window(final_forecast$mean, start = c(2026, 10), end = c(2026, 12)))
mean(window(candy_ts, start = c(2025, 10), end = c(2025, 12)))
```

**Conclusion:** ARIMA(3,0,0)(1,1,1)[12] has the lowest average error across the ten one-year tests (RMSE 5.95) and the cleanest residuals of the six models. It forecasts an average index of 84.3 for Sep 2026 – Aug 2027, 4.8% below the last 12 months, with an Oct–Dec 2026 holiday peak averaging 93.2, down 8% from 2025.
